country.name: Azerbaijan
country.tagline: German colonists' cellars at Göygöl, the pink Madrasa grape of Shamakhi and a state-backed revival.

stats.note: No reliable current vineyard figure found; Soviet Azerbaijan harvested about 2 million tonnes of grapes by the early 1980s. Wine output is small and not reported by OIV 2025.

country.overview:
Azerbaijan's wine history is ancient (jars with wine residues of the second millennium BC from Göygöl and Neolithic Kültəpə in Nakhchivan) and recent in equal measure. In 1817 to 1819 Lutheran colonists from Württemberg settled in the South Caucasus with the tsar's permission and founded Helenendorf (today Göygöl) near Ganja and Annenfeld (today Shamkir); families such as the Vohrer brothers and the Hummels built wineries and cognac houses that sold across the Russian Empire. Stalin deported the German community in 1941, but its cellars, including the Göygöl wine plant of 1860, are still in use.

Under the Soviet Union Azerbaijan became one of the biggest grape producers in the USSR, reaching about two million tonnes of grapes by the early 1980s, before Gorbachev's 1985 campaign tore out most of the vines. A state programme from 2012 to 2020 subsidised replanting, and a dozen modern wineries now work in three areas: Ganja and Göygöl, Tovuz and Shamkir in the west, and the Shamakhi and Ismayilli foothills of the Greater Caucasus in the east, where Savalan (Aspi Winery), Chabiant and Meysari make the best-known wines. The local signature is Madrasa (Matrassa), a dark-skinned grape named after the village of Madrasa near Shamakhi, used for deeply coloured dry and sweet reds. Nagorno-Karabakh, internationally recognised as part of Azerbaijan, had Armenian-run wineries (in Hadrut, Martuni and elsewhere, using the local Sireni grape) until the region's ethnic Armenian population left after Azerbaijan's military takeover in September 2023.

history.title: Ancient jars at Göygöl
history.text: Archaeologists found jars with wine remains in the Göygöl district dated to the second millennium BC.

history.title: The Swabian colonies
history.text: Colonists from Württemberg founded Helenendorf (Göygöl) and Annenfeld (Shamkir); their wineries industrialised Azerbaijani wine.

history.title: Deportation of the Germans
history.text: Stalin deported the Caucasus Germans to Central Asia; their cellars passed to Soviet state wineries.

history.title: The vines torn out
history.text: Gorbachev's anti-alcohol campaign destroyed most of Azerbaijan's Soviet-era vineyard.

history.title: State replanting programme
history.text: A national grape and wine programme subsidised new vineyards and wineries such as Savalan, Chabiant and Meysari.

country.climate_soils: Continental to subtropical, with semi-arid lowlands along the Kura and cooler foothills of the Greater and Lesser Caucasus at 300 to 900 metres; brown and chestnut soils, with winter burying of vines in colder sites.

grapes.name: Madrasa (Matrassa)
grapes.note: Dark local red from Shamakhi, also grown in Georgia and Armenia.

grapes.name: Bayan Shira
grapes.note: Local white, used for still and fortified wines.

grapes.name: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Pinot Noir, Chardonnay

further_reading: Wine and Wagons: Helenendorf, Azerbaijan's First German Settlement (Azerbaijan International)

sites.name: Göygöl wine plant (Helenendorf)
sites.text: Göygöl, founded as Helenendorf in 1819 by Swabian colonists, kept its German houses, Lutheran church and the wine and cognac plant founded in 1860, today run by Vinagro.

sites.name: Madrasa village
sites.text: Village near Shamakhi that gave its name to the Madrasa (Matrassa) grape, the signature red of eastern Azerbaijan.

sites.name: Savalan (Aspi Winery)
sites.text: Aspi Winery's estate at Savalan in the Qabala district, at the foot of the Greater Caucasus, established in the late 2000s; its Savalan wines are Azerbaijan's best-known exports.

sites.name: Chabiant
sites.text: Winery in Ismayilli district at the foot of the Greater Caucasus, making Madrasa and international varieties.
